correctness.rationale: Headline vanishing follows logically IF cited theorems are taken as black boxes. Lemma 1 (Sol(5)~=Sol(3) via v2(24)=v2(8)=3, l=0) is supported by HLL Sec.1.3/Thm 4.1 statement F_Sol(q)~=F_Sol(3^{2^l}) where 2^{l+3}||q^2-1; replayed v2/mod-8 arithmetic is correct. Lemma 2 (HLL Thm 1.1 punctured=>sharp for all i>=1,j>=0 including j=0, plus Thm 1.4 punctured iff q=+/-3 mod 8) accurately describes HLL; 5=-3 mod 8 so F_Sol(5) qualifies directly. Lemma 3 (sharpness transports along fusion-system isomorphism via orbit-category equivalence) is standard and sketch is sound; DRAFT honestly retracts false S-terminal shortcut with counter-witness. SNF artifacts (3x2 Cech toy matrix, 1x1 zero matrices) prove nothing about Sol(5) but DRAFT discloses vanishing is by transport not SNF, so no falsified certificate. Assemblative dependence on unre-verified HLL/COS08/Bova proofs is disclosed as limitation; no essential inference within scope is mathematically invalid.

originality.rationale: FAIL: headline Sol(5) sharpness is substantively already contained in HLL 2201.07160. HLL Thm 1.1 (punctured=>sharp, all i>=1,j>=0) combined with Thm 1.4/4.1 (F_Sol(q) has punctured group iff q=+/-3 mod 8, with F_Sol(q)~=F_Sol(3^{2^l})) directly entails sharpness for q=5 since 5=-3 mod 8 and l=0 (2-part of 24 is 8). DRAFT itself concedes this direct route (Remark: 'q=5 itself satisfies HLL criterion...with no transport needed'). Absence of string 'Sol(5)' in HLL title/abstract does not establish novelty; substantive theorem covers q=5 as member of infinite l=0 family. Iso-transport Sol(5)~=Sol(3) is therefore proof of the same object twice under different names, not a new case. Admission's premise that Sol(5) lacked punctured group / was first open case is factually wrong (confuses isomorphism type l>0 with parameter q=5); no prior gap existed. Result is mechanical instantiation (q=5) of published general theorem, not a new theorem.

value.rationale: FAIL: even taken as correct, result is mere parameter substitution with no independent retrieval value. Future researcher needing Sol(5) sharpness cites HLL Thms 1.1+1.4 directly (q=+/-3 mod 8 family); a note restating it for q=5 adds no lemma, method, computation, or boundary extension. Transport lemma is textbook category equivalence; Bova four-term collapse is automatic given vanishing; SNF fragment is generic toy matrices, not Sol(5)-specific data. Does not satisfy narrow-exact-invariant exception because value was already known/mechanically implied by HLL general theorem, not unknown. The admitted target's value rested on false open-gap premise; with gap closed by HLL, no standalone value remains.
